01.r: With the participle 'drawing near', forms a continuing past action.
01.n: The Greek opens with this verb, 'were', and joins it to the participle later in the sentence: 'were ... drawing near'. The combination pictures an ongoing scene, which the ASV and YLT keep and the KJV's 'drew near' does not.

03.r: Jesus, the one they are coming to.
03.n: The Greek puts this word right after 'were', ahead of the participle; the Textus Receptus puts it after the participle. See the note on the text.

04.r: They keep coming close to Jesus.
04.n: Abbott-Smith gives the intransitive sense 'to come near' and lists this verse for its use with the dative of the one approached.

05.r: The whole company of them, not a few.
05.n: 'All' may be a broad way of saying a great many; that is a reasonable reading, not something the text marks. The DRC leaves the word out.

06.r: The toll collectors as a known group.

07.r: Men of the toll trade, drawn to Jesus.
07.n: This study renders the word 'toll collector' throughout.

09.r: A second article: the sinners as their own group.
09.n: Each group has its own article here; only the YLT keeps the second.

11.r: Their purpose: to listen to his teaching.
11.n: Abbott-Smith gives 'to hear, listen, attend'. A present infinitive of purpose.

12.r: Jesus, the one they listen to.

tr_note: The Textus Receptus has αὐτῷ, 'to him', after the participle 'drawing near' instead of before it. The meaning is the same, and the difference does not show in the KJV.
